summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, Fujio Taniguchi completed a PhD at Nagoya University in 1991 under Musashi Tachikawa and others. He was a professor at Nagoya Women's University and taught at Aichi Gakuin University.

Fulgence Fresnel (1795–1855) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy around 1823–1826 and attended the Pontifical Maronite College (Maronite College) in 1826.

Fumi Yao is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Tokyo in 2011. She served as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo and as a part-time lecturer at Taisho University.

Fumihiko Sueki is a Buddhist studies and religious philosophy scholar who earned his degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo (1995–2009), the International Research Center for Japanese Studies, and SOKENDAI.

Fumihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 2015) and has served as a specially appointed associate professor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Fumimaro Watanabe (1934–1990) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Toronto under A. K. Warder. He was a professor at Kindai University (1981) and Aichi Gakuin University (1987).

Fumio Enomoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University from around 1980 to 1984 and as a professor at Osaka University from roughly 1999 to 2019.

Fumio Masutani (1902–1987) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He was a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and Taisho University, and president of Tsuru University.

Fumio Matsuda is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who held a post at Komazawa University and served as an executive committee chair for the Association for the Study of Indian Religions in 1997.

Fumio Ouchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history who received a doctorate in literature from Otani University. He served as an assistant professor (~1990–2000) and full professor (~2000–2013) at Otani University.

Fumio Shoji is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from 1998 to 2007. He was an assistant professor there from 2014 to 2019 and became an associate professor in 2019.
Fumio Tamamuro is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Meiji University between 1954 and 1964 and held a post there from around 1972 to 2006.

Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kyushu University around 1990–1991 and held posts at Shimane Prefectural Junior College of Nursing and Shimane International Junior College.

Futoshi Takehashi, a Buddhist studies scholar, completed doctoral coursework at Otani University (attested 1992). He served as an assistant at the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute from 1995 to 1997.
Fuyuan Luo is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. Supervised by Adam Yuet Chau, Luo is a PhD student and holds a post at the University of Cambridge.

Fyodor Buslaev (1818–1897) was a linguist and historian who studied at Moscow State University under Pavel Jakovlevič Petrov. He later served as an adjunkt and faculty member at Moscow State University starting in 1846 and 1850.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (1866–1942) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Saint Petersburg, Vienna, and Bonn under Minaev, Oldenburg, Bühler, and Jacobi, and served as docent and professor at Saint Petersburg State University (1901–1930).

Félicien de Saulcy (1807–1880) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied under Eugène Burnouf and attended the École polytechnique (1826–1828) and the École d'application de l'artillerie et du génie in Metz (1828–1830).

Félix Lacôte (1873–1925) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi at the University of Paris. He served as Foucher's deputy at the EPHE and became professor at the University of Lyon in 1911.

Félix Nève (1816–1893) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at KU Leuven, Bonn, Munich, and Paris under Burnouf, Lassen, and Thiersch. He served as a professor at KU Leuven from 1841 until 1877.
